part.text:
Fixed. The root cause was in `OrderedMap.__iterate` (src/OrderedMap.js:64): it returned the count from `List.__iterate`, which includes tombstone "holes" left behind by `remove()` on the underlying list. That inflated iteration count propagated to `hashCollection` (src/CollectionImpl.js:753), giving `OrderedSet`/`OrderedMap` instances with identical contents different `hashCode()` values depending on whether entries had been removed.

The fix counts only real entries during iteration, so `OrderedSet(['hello'])` and `OrderedSet(['goodbye', 'hello']).remove('goodbye')` now share the same hashCode (and equality, which uses the same iteration count in `compareUnorderedCollections`). All 44 test suites / 685 tests pass, including the new `hashCode should return the same value if the values are the same` case in `__tests__/OrderedSet.ts`, and lint/prettier are clean.
